name: Imatinib (Gleevec)
dosage: 400mg orally once daily for chronic phase CML; 600mg daily for accelerated phase; 800mg daily for blast crisis
description: First-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that targets BCR-ABL fusion protein. Revolutionized CML treatment with 85% complete cytogenetic response rates. FDA-approved in 2001.
monitoring: Complete blood count weekly for first month, then monthly
Molecular response assessment (BCR-ABL PCR) every 3 months
administration: Take with food and large glass of water. Avoid grapefruit juice.

name: Dasatinib (Sprycel)
dosage: 100mg orally once daily for chronic phase CML; 140mg daily for accelerated phase/blast crisis; 140mg daily for Ph+ ALL
description: Second-generation TKI 325 times more potent than imatinib against BCR-ABL. Active against most imatinib-resistant mutations except T315I. FDA-approved in 2006.
monitoring: Complete blood count weekly for 2 months
administration: Take with or without food. Avoid antacids 2 hours before/after.

name: Nilotinib (Tasigna)
dosage: 300mg orally twice daily on empty stomach (no food 2 hours before or 1 hour after)
description: Second-generation TKI with high potency and specificity for BCR-ABL. Requires fasting administration. FDA-approved in 2007.
monitoring: ECG baseline and 7 days after dose initiation
administration: Take on empty stomach - no food 2 hours before or 1 hour after. Avoid grapefruit.

name: Bosutinib (Bosulif)
dosage: 500mg orally once daily
description: Second-generation TKI targeting both BCR-ABL and Src family kinases. FDA-approved in 2012 for chronic, accelerated, or blast phase CML.
monitoring: Complete blood count weekly for first month
administration: Take with food. Dose reduce for liver impairment.

name: Ponatinib (Iclusig)
dosage: 45mg orally once daily; reduce to 15mg daily after response
description: Third-generation TKI active against T315I mutation and all other BCR-ABL mutations. Black box warning for arterial thrombosis. FDA-approved in 2012.
administration: Take with or without food. Reduce dose for hepatic impairment.

name: Asciminib (Scemblix)
dosage: 80mg orally once daily or 40mg twice daily
description: First-in-class STAMP inhibitor targeting ABL myristoyl pocket. Novel mechanism distinct from ATP-competitive TKIs. FDA-approved in 2021 for CML after >=2 TKIs.
administration: Take with or without food. Can be used with other TKIs in combination.
drugClass: STAMP Inhibitor (Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket)

name: Cytarabine (Ara-C)
dosage: Standard: 100-200mg/m²/day IV continuous infusion x 7 days; High-dose: 1-3g/m² every 12 hours x 2-6 doses
description: Antimetabolite that inhibits DNA polymerase. Cornerstone of AML induction therapy (7+3 regimen). FDA-approved for AML and ALL treatment since 1969.
administration: IV infusion over 1-3 hours (standard) or 1-3 hours (high-dose). Pre-medicate with antiemetics.

name: Daunorubicin (Cerubidine)
dosage: 45-90mg/m² IV daily x 3 days (standard 7+3); 60mg/m² (liposomal formulation)
description: Anthracycline antibiotic that intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II. Standard component of AML induction (7+3 regimen). FDA-approved since 1979.
administration: IV infusion over 5-15 minutes. Monitor for extravasation.

name: Idarubicin (Idamycin)
dosage: 12mg/m² IV daily x 3 days (often combined with cytarabine)
description: Anthracycline analog more lipophilic and potent than daunorubicin. Better tissue penetration. FDA-approved for AML since 1990.
administration: IV infusion over 5-15 minutes. Monitor for extravasation.

name: Mitoxantrone (Novantrone)
dosage: 12mg/m² IV daily x 3 days (combined with cytarabine)
description: Anthracycline analog with less cardiotoxicity than doxorubicin. Used in AML induction and consolidation. FDA-approved for AML and ALL.
administration: IV infusion over 5-15 minutes. Monitor for extravasation.

name: Aclarubicin (Aclacinomycin)
dosage: 20mg/m² IV daily x 7 days (induction)
description: Anthracycline antibiotic with lower cardiotoxicity. Used in AML induction therapy. FDA-approved for AML.
administration: IV infusion over 5-15 minutes. Monitor for extravasation.

name: Midostaurin (Rydapt)
dosage: 50mg orally twice daily with food on days 8-21 of each 28-day cycle (combined with chemotherapy)
description: Multi-kinase inhibitor targeting FLT3, PKC, and others. First FLT3 inhibitor approved for AML. FDA-approved in 2017 for newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML.
administration: Take with food. Continue through consolidation cycles.

name: Gilteritinib (Xospata)
dosage: 120mg orally once daily
description: Potent FLT3/AXL inhibitor. FDA-approved in 2018 for relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML. Higher response rates than chemotherapy.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Quizartinib (Vanflyta)
dosage: 40mg orally once daily (days 1-14), then 80mg once daily (days 15-28) of 28-day cycle
description: Potent FLT3 inhibitor with activity against FLT3-ITD mutations. FDA-approved in 2023 for relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML.
administration: Take with or without food. ECG monitoring required.

name: Crenolanib
dosage: 100mg orally twice daily
description: Potent FLT3 inhibitor active against FLT3-ITD and TKD mutations. FDA-approved in 2023 for FLT3-mutated AML.
administration: Take with or without food. Blood pressure monitoring essential.

name: Ivosidenib (Tibsovo)
dosage: 500mg orally once daily with or without food
description: IDH1 inhibitor that blocks production of 2-hydroxyglutarate. FDA-approved in 2018 for relapsed/refractory IDH1-mutated AML and newly diagnosed IDH1-mutated AML.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Enasidenib (Idhifa)
dosage: 100mg orally once daily with or without food
description: IDH2 inhibitor that blocks production of 2-hydroxyglutarate. FDA-approved in 2017 for relapsed/refractory IDH2-mutated AML.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Venetoclax (Venclexta)
dosage: Ramp-up: 20mg->50mg->100mg->200mg->400mg daily over 5 days; Maintenance: 400mg daily (with azacitidine/decitabine or low-dose cytarabine)
description: BCL-2 inhibitor that promotes apoptosis in cancer cells. FDA-approved in 2018 for AML (with hypomethylating agents) and 2016 for CLL. Particularly effective in elderly/unfit AML patients.
contraindications: Tumor lysis syndrome risk without prophylaxis
administration: Ramp-up over 5 days to prevent TLS. Take with food and water. TLS prophylaxis required.

name: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg)
dosage: 3mg/m² IV on days 1, 4, and 7 (fractionated dosing) or 6mg/m² IV on day 1 (single dose)
description: CD33-directed antibody-drug conjugate with calicheamicin. FDA-approved in 2000, withdrawn in 2010, re-approved in 2017 for CD33-positive AML.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours. Pre-medicate with corticosteroids and antihistamines.

name: Blinatumomab (Blincyto)
dosage: Continuous IV infusion: 9µg/day days 1-7, then 28µg/day days 8-28 (cycle 1); 28µg/day days 1-28 (subsequent cycles)
description: Bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) targeting CD19 on B-cells and CD3 on T-cells. FDA-approved in 2014 for relapsed/refractory B-cell ALL and MRD-positive ALL.
administration: Continuous IV infusion via pump. Hospitalization required for first cycle. Pre-medicate with dexamethasone.

name: Inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa)
dosage: 0.8mg/m² on day 1 (0.5mg/m² on cycle 1), 0.5mg/m² on days 8 and 15, repeated every 28 days
description: CD22-directed antibody-drug conjugate with calicheamicin. FDA-approved in 2017 for relapsed/refractory B-cell ALL. High remission rates but significant hepatotoxicity.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Pre-medicate with corticosteroids and antihistamines.

name: Tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah)
dosage: 0.2-5 x 10^6 CAR T cells/kg IV infusion (single dose after lymphodepletion)
description: CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy. FDA-approved in 2017 for patients <=25 years with B-cell ALL that is refractory or in second/later relapse. Revolutionary cellular therapy.
administration: Single IV infusion after lymphodepletion chemotherapy. Requires specialized center.
storage: Cryopreserved at -150°C to -180°C. Thaw before infusion.

name: Brexucabtagene autoleucel (Tecartus)
dosage: 0.2-5 x 10^6 CAR T cells/kg IV infusion (single dose after lymphodepletion)
description: CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy. FDA-approved in 2021 for adult B-cell ALL in relapse or refractory. Similar to Kymriah but for adult population.
administration: Single IV infusion after lymphodepletion chemotherapy. Requires specialized center.
storage: Cryopreserved at -150°C to -180°C. Thaw before infusion.

name: Asparaginase (Pegaspargase)
dosage: 2500 IU/m² IM or IV every 2 weeks; 2000 IU/m² for pegylated formulation
description: Enzyme that depletes asparagine, essential for ALL cells. Critical component of ALL induction and consolidation. FDA-approved pegylated formulation reduces immunogenicity.
administration: IM or IV infusion. Monitor for allergic reactions during first administration.

name: Calaspargase pegol (Asparlas)
dosage: 2500 IU/m² IV every 3 weeks
description: Pegylated E. coli-derived L-asparaginase with longer half-life and reduced immunogenicity. FDA-approved in 2018 for ALL.
administration: IV infusion every 3 weeks. Monitor for allergic reactions.

name: Vincristine
dosage: 1.4mg/m² IV weekly (max 2mg per dose)
description: Vinca alkaloid that disrupts microtubule formation, preventing cell division. Standard component of ALL induction (VCR in VDLP regimen). FDA-approved since 1963.
administration: IV injection over 1 minute. Avoid extravasation.

name: Vinblastine
dosage: 6mg/m² IV weekly
description: Vinca alkaloid similar to vincristine but with different toxicity profile. Used in various leukemia protocols.
administration: IV injection over 1 minute. Avoid extravasation.

name: Vinorelbine
dosage: 25-30mg/m² IV weekly or 60-80mg/m² orally weekly
description: Semi-synthetic vinca alkaloid with oral and IV formulations. Used in various hematologic malignancies.
administration: IV infusion over 6-10 minutes or oral capsules. Avoid extravasation.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Dexamethasone
dosage: 6-10mg/m² orally daily in divided doses (induction/consolidation for ALL)
description: Potent corticosteroid with anti-leukemic and anti-inflammatory effects. Standard component of ALL induction. More potent than prednisone with better CNS penetration.
administration: Oral tablets or IV injection. Taper dose when discontinuing.

name: Prednisone
dosage: 40-60mg/m² orally daily divided doses (ALL induction)
description: Corticosteroid with anti-leukemic effects. Standard component of ALL induction regimens. Less potent than dexamethasone but with different side effect profile.
administration: Oral tablets. Take with food to reduce GI upset.

name: Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol)
dosage: 1-2mg/kg IV or orally daily divided doses
description: Intermediate-acting corticosteroid with potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Used in various leukemia protocols.
administration: IV infusion or oral tablets. Taper dose when discontinuing.

name: Prednisolone
dosage: 40-60mg/m² orally daily divided doses (ALL induction)
description: Corticosteroid similar to prednisone but with different pharmacokinetics. Used in various leukemia protocols.
administration: Oral tablets or IV injection. Take with food to reduce GI upset.

name: Hydrocortisone
dosage: 200-300mg/m² IV divided doses every 6 hours
description: Short-acting corticosteroid with both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid activity. Used in leukemia protocols and adrenal insufficiency.
administration: IV infusion or oral tablets. Monitor electrolytes closely.

name: Ibrutinib (Imbruvica)
dosage: 420mg orally once daily for CLL/MCL; 560mg daily for WM/MZL
description: Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor. First BTK inhibitor approved. FDA-approved in 2013 for CLL and other B-cell malignancies. Oral therapy with good efficacy.
administration: Take with water. Can be taken with or without food.

name: Acalabrutinib (Calquence)
dosage: 100mg orally twice daily
description: Second-generation BTK inhibitor with more selective BTK inhibition and fewer off-target effects than ibrutinib. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: Take approximately 12 hours apart. Can be taken with or without food.

name: Zanubrutinib (Brukinsa)
dosage: 160mg orally twice daily or 320mg once daily
description: Next-generation BTK inhibitor designed for more complete BTK inhibition and better selectivity. FDA-approved in 2019 for MCL and 2020 for CLL.
administration: Can be taken with or without food. Consistent timing recommended.

name: Idelalisib (Zydelig)
dosage: 150mg orally twice daily
description: PI3Kdelta inhibitor. First PI3K inhibitor approved for hematologic malignancies. FDA-approved in 2014. Significant toxicity profile limits use.
administration: Take with or without food. Anti-diarrheal prophylaxis recommended.

name: Duvelisib (Copiktra)
dosage: 25mg orally twice daily
description: PI3Kdelta/gamma dual inhibitor. FDA-approved in 2018 for CLL/SLL after >=2 prior therapies and FL after >=2 prior therapies. Broader PI3K inhibition.
administration: Take with or without food. Anti-diarrheal prophylaxis recommended.

name: Copanlisib (Aliqopa)
dosage: 60mg IV over 1 hour on days 1, 8, and 15 of 28-day cycle
description: PI3Kalpha/delta inhibitor with IV administration. FDA-approved in 2017 for relapsed follicular lymphoma after >=2 prior therapies.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Monitor blood glucose and blood pressure.

name: Umbralisib (Ukoniq)
dosage: 800mg orally once daily
description: PI3Kdelta/CK1epsilon inhibitor with improved safety profile. FDA-approved in 2021 for CLL/SLL after >=1 prior therapy and FL after >=2 prior therapies.
administration: Take with or without food. Anti-diarrheal prophylaxis recommended.

name: Hydroxyurea (Hydrea)
dosage: 500-1000mg orally daily divided doses
description: Antimetabolite that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase. Used for chronic phase CML and cytoreduction in other leukemias.
administration: Take with food to reduce GI upset. Increase fluid intake.

name: Azacitidine (Vidaza)
dosage: 75mg/m² subcutaneously or IV daily x 7 days every 28 days
description: Hypomethylating agent that incorporates into DNA and RNA. FDA-approved for MDS and AML. Used in elderly/unfit patients.
administration: Subcutaneous injection or IV infusion. Antiemetic premedication recommended.

name: Decitabine (Dacogen)
dosage: 20mg/m² IV over 1 hour daily x 5 days every 28 days
description: Hypomethylating agent that incorporates into DNA. FDA-approved for MDS and AML. Similar to azacitidine but DNA-specific.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Antiemetic premedication recommended.

name: Clofarabine (Clolar)
dosage: 52mg/m² IV over 2 hours daily x 5 days (pediatric ALL); 52mg/m² IV over 2 hours daily x 5 days (AML)
description: Second-generation purine nucleoside analog. FDA-approved for pediatric ALL and AML. Potent antimetabolite activity.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours. Aggressive hydration and antiemetic prophylaxis required.

name: Fludarabine (Fludara)
dosage: 25mg/m² IV over 30 minutes daily x 5 days (CLL); 25mg/m² IV over 30 minutes daily x 5 days (AML/ALL)
description: Purine nucleoside analog that inhibits DNA synthesis. FDA-approved for CLL. Used in various leukemia protocols.
administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes. Aggressive hydration required.

name: Cladribine (Leustatin)
dosage: 0.14mg/kg continuous IV infusion over 2 hours daily x 5 days (CLL)
description: Purine nucleoside analog with activity against lymphoid malignancies. FDA-approved for hairy cell leukemia and CLL.
administration: Continuous IV infusion over 2 hours. Hydration required.

name: Nelarabine (Arranon)
dosage: 650mg/m² IV over 1 hour daily x 5 days (adult); 650mg/m² IV over 1 hour daily x 5 days (pediatric)
description: Prodrug of ara-G, active against T-cell malignancies. FDA-approved for T-ALL and T-LBL. Specific for T-cell leukemias.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Neurological monitoring essential.

name: Busulfan (Busulfex)
dosage: 0.8mg/kg IV every 6 hours x 4 days (conditioning); 1-2mg/kg orally daily (maintenance)
description: Alkylating agent used for conditioning before stem cell transplant and CML treatment. FDA-approved for CML.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours or oral capsules. Seizure prophylaxis required for IV formulation.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Melphalan (Alkeran)
dosage: 100-200mg/m² IV over 30 minutes (high-dose); 0.1-0.2mg/kg orally daily (low-dose)
description: Alkylating agent used in conditioning regimens and leukemia treatment. FDA-approved for multiple myeloma and used off-label for leukemias.
administration: IV infusion or oral tablets. Aggressive hydration required for high-dose.

name: Cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan)
dosage: 50-60mg/kg IV over 1 hour daily x 2 days (high-dose); 1-5mg/kg orally daily (low-dose)
description: Alkylating agent widely used in leukemia protocols and conditioning regimens. FDA-approved for various malignancies.
administration: IV infusion or oral tablets. Aggressive hydration required for IV dosing.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Ifosfamide (Ifex)
dosage: 1.2-2.0g/m² IV over 30-60 minutes daily x 5 days
description: Alkylating agent similar to cyclophosphamide but with different toxicity profile. Used in ALL protocols.
administration: IV infusion with mesna uroprotection. Aggressive hydration required.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Chlorambucil (Leukeran)
dosage: 0.1-0.2mg/kg orally daily (CLL maintenance)
description: Alkylating agent with oral bioavailability. Used for CLL maintenance and CML treatment. FDA-approved for CLL.
administration: Oral tablets. Take with food to reduce GI upset.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Ibrutinib (Imbruvica)
dosage: 420mg orally once daily for CLL; 560mg daily for MCL
description: First-in-class Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor. Revolutionized CLL treatment. FDA-approved in 2014 for CLL.
administration: Take with water. Can be taken with or without food.

name: Venetoclax (Venclexta)
dosage: Ramp-up to 400mg daily for CLL; 400-800mg daily for AML
description: BCL-2 inhibitor that induces apoptosis in cancer cells. Used in CLL and AML. FDA-approved in 2016.
administration: Ramp-up dosing over 5 weeks with TLS prophylaxis. Take with food and water.

name: Acalabrutinib (Calquence)
dosage: 100mg orally twice daily
description: Second-generation BTK inhibitor with more selective targeting and better safety profile than ibrutinib. FDA-approved in 2019.
administration: Take with or without food. Swallow whole with water.

name: Azacitidine (Vidaza)
dosage: 75mg/m² subcutaneously or IV daily x 7 days every 28 days
description: Hypomethylating agent that incorporates into DNA and RNA. Used for AML and MDS. FDA-approved since 2004.
administration: Subcutaneous injection or IV infusion. Antiemetic premedication recommended.
storage: Reconstituted solution stable for 8 hours refrigerated. Protect from light.

name: Gilteritinib (Xospata)
dosage: 120mg orally once daily
description: FLT3 inhibitor for relapsed/refractory AML with FLT3 mutations. FDA-approved in 2018.
administration: Take with or without food. Swallow whole.

name: Midostaurin (Rydapt)
dosage: 50mg orally twice daily with food
description: Multi-kinase inhibitor targeting FLT3. Used for AML with FLT3 mutations and systemic mastocytosis. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: Take with food to improve absorption. Swallow whole.

name: Ivosidenib (Tibsovo)
dosage: 500mg orally once daily
description: IDH1 inhibitor for AML with IDH1 mutations. First targeted therapy for IDH-mutated AML. FDA-approved in 2018.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Enasidenib (Idhifa)
dosage: 100mg orally once daily
description: IDH2 inhibitor for AML with IDH2 mutations. Targeted therapy for IDH-mutated AML. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Nelarabine (Arranon)
dosage: 650mg/m² IV over 1 hour daily x 5 days every 21 days
description: Prodrug of ara-G, a deoxyguanosine analog toxic to T-cells. Used for T-ALL and T-LBL. FDA-approved in 2005.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Pre-medicate with antiemetics.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Asparaginase (Elspar)
dosage: 6,000-10,000 IU/m² IM or IV 3 times weekly
description: Enzyme that depletes asparagine, essential for leukemic cell survival. Cornerstone of ALL therapy. FDA-approved since 1978.
administration: IM or IV infusion. Monitor for anaphylaxis during first doses.

name: Pegaspargase (Oncaspar)
dosage: 2,500 IU/m² IM or IV every 14 days
description: Pegylated form of asparaginase with longer half-life and reduced immunogenicity. FDA-approved in 1994.
administration: IM or IV infusion over 1-2 hours. Monitor for anaphylaxis.

name: Calaspargase Pegol (Asparlas)
dosage: 2,500 IU/m² IV every 3 weeks
description: Pegylated asparaginase with extended dosing interval. FDA-approved in 2018 for ALL.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Extended dosing schedule reduces clinic visits.

name: Clofarabine (Clolar)
dosage: 52mg/m² IV over 2 hours daily x 5 days
description: Second-generation purine nucleoside analog. Used for relapsed/refractory ALL and AML. FDA-approved in 2004.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours. Aggressive hydration and antiemetics required.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Inotuzumab Ozogamicin (Besponsa)
dosage: 1.8mg/m² IV weekly x 3-4 doses per cycle
description: Anti-CD22 antibody-drug conjugate with calicheamicin. Used for relapsed/refractory B-ALL. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Monitor for infusion reactions.

name: Blinatumomab (Blincyto)
dosage: 9mcg/day continuous IV infusion days 1-7, then 28mcg/day days 8-28
description: Bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) targeting CD19. Connects T-cells to CD19+ leukemia cells. FDA-approved in 2014.
administration: Continuous IV infusion via pump. Hospitalization for first 9 days recommended.

name: Tisagenlecleucel (Kymriah)
dosage: 0.2-5 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg IV single infusion
description: CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy. Patient's T-cells engineered to target CD19. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: IV infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy. Hospitalization required.
storage: Cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen. Thawed immediately before infusion.

name: Decitabine (Dacogen)
dosage: 20mg/m² IV over 1 hour daily x 5 days every 28 days
description: Hypomethylating agent that incorporates into DNA. Used for AML and MDS. FDA-approved in 2006.
administration: IV infusion over 1 hour. Antiemetic premedication recommended.
storage: Reconstituted solution stable for 8 hours refrigerated. Protect from light.

name: Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin (Mylotarg)
dosage: 3mg/m² IV on days 1, 4, and 7 (fractionated dosing)
description: Anti-CD33 antibody-drug conjugate with calicheamicin. Used for CD33+ AML. FDA-approved in 2000, withdrawn 2010, re-approved 2017.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours. Monitor for infusion reactions.

name: Daunorubicin and Cytarabine Liposome (Vyxeos)
dosage: 44mg/m² daunorubicin + 100mg/m² cytarabine IV over 90 minutes days 1, 4, 7
description: Liposomal formulation of daunorubicin and cytarabine in fixed 1:5 molar ratio. Used for therapy-related AML and AML-MRC. FDA-approved in 2017.
administration: IV infusion over 90 minutes. First dose may require cardiac monitoring.

name: Quizartinib (Vanflyta)
dosage: 60mg orally once daily (days 8-21 of 28-day cycle)
description: FLT3 inhibitor for FLT3-ITD mutated AML. Potent FLT3 inhibition. FDA-approved in 2023.
administration: Take with food. ECG monitoring required during initiation.

name: Olutasidenib (Rezlidhia)
dosage: 150mg orally twice daily
description: IDH1 inhibitor for AML with IDH1 mutations. Targeted therapy for IDH-mutated AML. FDA-approved in 2022.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.

name: Arsenic Trioxide (Trisenox)
dosage: 0.15mg/kg IV daily until remission, then consolidation
description: Induces degradation of PML-RARα fusion protein. Used for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). FDA-approved in 2000.
administration: IV infusion over 1-4 hours. Correct electrolytes before starting.

name: Tretinoin (Vesanoid)
dosage: 45mg/m² orally daily divided into 2 doses
description: Induces differentiation of promyelocytes. Used for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). FDA-approved in 1995.
administration: Oral capsules with food. Monitor for differentiation syndrome.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Revumenib (Revuforj)
dosage: 163mg orally twice daily
description: Menin-MLL inhibitor for KMT2A-rearranged or NPM1-mutated leukemia. First-in-class menin inhibitor. FDA-approved in 2022.
administration: Take with or without food. ECG monitoring required.

name: Zanubrutinib (Brukinsa)
dosage: 160mg orally twice daily
description: Second-generation BTK inhibitor with more selective targeting. FDA-approved in 2019 for MCL, 2023 for CLL.
administration: Take with water. Can be taken with or without food.

name: Pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca)
dosage: 200mg orally once daily
description: Third-generation BTK inhibitor effective after covalent BTK inhibitor failure. FDA-approved in 2023.
administration: Take with or without food. Swallow whole with water.

name: Idelalisib (Zydelig)
dosage: 150mg orally twice daily
description: PI3Kδ inhibitor that blocks B-cell receptor signaling. FDA-approved in 2014 for relapsed CLL.
administration: Take with food. Monitor for diarrhea and colitis.

name: Duvelisib (Copiktra)
dosage: 25mg orally twice daily
description: PI3Kδ/γ dual inhibitor. Used for CLL after at least 2 prior therapies. FDA-approved in 2018.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor for diarrhea and colitis.

name: Obinutuzumab (Gazyva)
dosage: 100mg IV on day 1, 900mg on day 8, 1000mg on day 15 (cycle 1), then 1000mg day 1
description: Type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody with enhanced direct cell death. FDA-approved in 2013.
administration: IV infusion with premedication. First infusion may require longer infusion time.

name: Ofatumumab (Arzerra)
dosage: 300mg IV week 0, 1000mg IV week 1, 1000mg IV week 2, then 1000mg IV every 4 weeks
description: Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody binding distinct epitope from rituximab. FDA-approved in 2009.
administration: IV infusion with premedication. Monitor for infusion reactions.

name: Alemtuzumab (Campath)
dosage: 30mg IV three times weekly for up to 12 weeks
description: Anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody causing profound lymphocyte depletion. FDA-approved in 2001 for CLL.
administration: IV infusion with premedication. Aggressive infection prophylaxis required.

name: Bendamustine (Treanda)
dosage: 100mg/m² IV over 30 minutes days 1 and 2 every 28 days
description: Bifunctional alkylating agent with benzimidazole ring. Used for CLL after rituximab failure. FDA-approved in 2008.
administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes. Antiemetic premedication recommended.

name: Fludarabine (Fludara)
dosage: 25mg/m² IV over 30 minutes daily x 5 days every 28 days
description: Purine analog that inhibits DNA synthesis. Used for CLL treatment. FDA-approved in 1991.
administration: IV infusion over 30 minutes. Monitor for autoimmune hemolysis.

name: Hydroxyurea (Hydrea)
dosage: 15-30mg/kg orally daily divided into 2-3 doses
description: Antimetabolite that inhibits ribonucleotide reductase. Used for CML cytoreduction and CLL. FDA-approved since 1967.
administration: Oral capsules with food. Dose adjust for renal impairment.

name: Busulfan (Myleran)
dosage: 1-2mg/kg orally daily (CML); 0.8mg/kg IV every 6 hours x 16 doses (conditioning)
description: Alkylating agent used for CML and stem cell transplant conditioning. FDA-approved since 1954.
administration: Oral tablets or IV infusion. Seizure prophylaxis required for high-dose IV.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from light.

name: Omacetaxine (Synribo)
dosage: 1.25mg/m² subcutaneously twice daily x 7 days every 28 days
description: Protein synthesis inhibitor. Used for CML after TKI failure. FDA-approved in 2012.
administration: Subcutaneous injection twice daily. Rotate injection sites.

name: Obecabtagene Autoleucel (Aucatzyl)
dosage: 1 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg IV single infusion
description: CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy. FDA-approved in 2021 for relapsed/refractory B-ALL.
administration: IV infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy. Hospitalization required.
storage: Cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen. Thawed immediately before infusion.

name: Lisocabtagene Maraleucel (Breyanzi)
dosage: 0.1-1 x 10^8 CAR-T cells/kg IV single infusion
description: CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy with defined CD4:CD8 ratio. FDA-approved in 2021.
administration: IV infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy. Hospitalization required.
storage: Cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen. Thawed immediately before infusion.

name: Pemigatinib (Pemazyre)
dosage: 13.5mg orally once daily
description: FGFR inhibitor for FGFR1/2/3 rearranged leukemias. Targeted therapy. FDA-approved in 2020.
administration: Take with or without food. Monitor phosphate levels.

name: Treosulfan (Grafapex)
dosage: 14g/m² IV over 2 hours daily x 3 days (conditioning)
description: Alkylating agent used for stem cell transplant conditioning. FDA-approved in 2022.
administration: IV infusion over 2 hours. Aggressive hydration required.
storage: Reconstituted solution stable for 8 hours at room temperature.

name: Vincristine Sulfate
dosage: 1.5-2mg/m² IV weekly (maximum 2mg)
description: Vinca alkaloid that disrupts microtubule formation. Used in multiple leukemia protocols. FDA-approved since 1963.
administration: IV infusion over 1 minute. Avoid intrathecal administration.

name: Methotrexate Sodium
dosage: 20-40mg/m² IV weekly; 12mg intrathecal for CNS prophylaxis
description: Folate analog that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase. Used in ALL and CNS prophylaxis. FDA-approved since 1953.
administration: IV, IM, or intrathecal. Leucovorin rescue for high-dose therapy.

name: Prednisone
dosage: 40-60mg/m² orally daily divided into 2-3 doses
description: Corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Used in all leukemia types. FDA-approved since 1955.
administration: Oral tablets with food to reduce GI upset. Taper dose gradually.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from moisture.

name: Dexamethasone
dosage: 6-10mg/m² orally daily divided into 2-3 doses
description: Potent corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Used in all leukemia types. FDA-approved since 1958.
administration: Oral tablets with food to reduce GI upset. Taper dose gradually.
storage: Store at room temperature 20-25°C (68-77°F). Protect from moisture.

name: Cyclophosphamide
dosage: 50-60mg/kg IV over 1-2 hours (conditioning); 600mg/m² IV daily (induction)
description: Alkylating agent used in all leukemia types and stem cell transplant. FDA-approved since 1959.
administration: IV infusion with aggressive hydration and MESNA for bladder protection.
